text: The regular meeting of the Society was almost wholly occupied with the subject of City Health Regulations.

label: real
text: Davis, from the Special Committee on that subject, made the following report, which, after free discussion, was adopted.

label: real
text: The Committee was instructed to present the same to the Common Council, with the draft of an amendment to the present laws, as indicated in the report.

label: real
text: REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE ON THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT OF OUR CITY GOVERNMENT.

label: real
text: Presen‘ed to the Chicago Medical Society, January 18th, 1867.

label: real
text: The subject assigned to your Committee for consideration, is certainly one of the most important that can engage the attention of the people of this, or any other large city.

label: real
text: The adoption and enforcement of proper sanitary regulations is so closely connected with the preservation of health and the prolongation of life and happiness, that no community can neglect them without, sooner or later, suffering the severest penalties.

label: real
text: In fulfilling the duties assigned to your Committee, three questions require careful consideration.

label: real
text: 1st.

label: real
text: What are principles upon which a Municipal Health Department should be organized, in order to ensure the highest degree of enlightment and efficient action?

label: real
text: Is the present organization of the Health Department of our city defective; and if so, in what particulars?

label: real
text: 1867. ] Editorial. 56

label: real
text: What changes are necessary to remedy its defects, and complete its efficiency ?

label: real
text: In answer to the first question, we would state, that the basis of a proper Health Organization, should consist of a Board of Commissioners, embodying in its members a high degree of executive ability or business capacity, and a thorough knowledge of sanitary science, as applied to the preservation of the health of communities and the prevention of the spread of contagious diseases.

label: real
text: No board can embody these qualities, without being composed in part, at least, of thoroughly-educated physicians; simply because, in our country, no other class of men are educated to an adequate extent, in reference to those sanitary subjects on which a Board of Health must continually act.

label: real
text: The truth of this proposition is too plain to need either argument or illustration.

label: real
text: A Board of Health Commissioners, composed of properly educated and qualified members, should be invested with sufficient power to devise and carry into prompt effect, all such measures as the safety and welfare of the community requires.

label: real
text: The term of office of its members should be long enough to insure a reasonable degree of permanency in whatever sanitary measures or policy may be adopted.

label: real
text: In no department of municipal affairs, is a vaccillating, temporizing policy more disastrous than in that relating to the preservation of the publie health.

label: real
text: A show of energy, or a display of zeal, or a prodigal expenditure of money just while some fearful epidemic disease is threatening to commence its work of death, and a negligent indifference at all other times, is but little better than no action at all.

label: real
text: Sanitary measures, to be successful in lessening the sickness and mortality of communities, and in protecting them from the ravages of epidemics, must be founded on an accurate knowledge of all those local causes that tend to deteriorate the public health, and then they must be rigidly and perseveringly enforced from year to year.

label: real
text: To enable a Board of Health Commissioners to devise such measures, and establish an enlightened and permanent sanitary policy, its members should not only possess the requisite educa-

label: real
text: 56 The Chicago Medical Examiner.

label: real
text: [Jan.

label: real
text: tion and business capacity, with a term of office long enough to add experience to their previous knowledge, but they should be appointed in such a manner as to free them as far as possible from all partisanship, or feelings of dependence on the success or failure of mere political parties.

label: real
text: And yet they should be fully accountable to the municipal government for all their official acts.

label: real
text: Such are the principles on which a Board of Health Commissioners should be organized.

label: real
text: The next question is, how far the present health department of our city government is organized in accordance with these principles, and in what particulars is it defective?

label: real
text: Our present Health Department consists of a Board of three Commissioners, who are also at the same time Commissioners of the Police and Fire Departments; a Health-Officer; and a City Physician.

label: real
text: The three members of the Board are elected by the people, one from each division of the city, and hold their offices for six years.

label: real
text: The Health-Officer is appointed by the Board.

label: real
text: The City Physician is elected by the Common Council, and holds oflice for two years.

label: real
text: The present city charter confers on the Common Council power ‘“‘to do all acts and make all regulations which may be necessary or expedient, for the preservation of health, and the suppression of disease.”’.

label: real
text: And, in accordance with this power, we find in the present laws and ordinances of the city full and ample powers conferred and duties enjoined upon the Board of of Health and Health-Officer, for the efficient and thorough regulation of everything relating to the public health and safety.

label: real
text: After a full examination of the present laws and ordinances, we can see no need of further legislation, so fur as relates to the conferring of power upon the Board of Health or its agents.

label: real
text: Wherein, then, is the present organization defective?

label: real
text: Chiefly . in three important particulars.

label: real
text: The first and most radical defect is, the absence of all provision for securing the selection of members of the Board of Health so thoroughly educated in sanitary matters as to fit them for an enlightened and efficient discharge of their duties.

label: real
text: To make up a Board of Health, charged

label: real
text: 1867. ] Editorial. aT

label: real
text: with the duty of making and enforcing all such regulations as are necessary to mitigate or prevent the prevalence of diseases in a great city, of men who, neither by education, occupation, nor business habits, have acquired any special knowledge of the nature and causes of disease, or of the laws by which they are developed and diffused, is just as absurd as it would be to elect a practising

label: real
text: physician to the office of City Attorney.

label: real
text: If there is lack of efficiency in the practical working of our present health organization, it is not because the members of the present Board of Police, acting as a Board of Health, are deficient in integrity or business capacity, or from deficient legal authority to-act, but simply because they have not that special sanitary or medical education which enables them to comprehend clearly the

label: real
text: nature, extent, and importance of the work entrusted to them.

label: real
text: The second defect consists in an imperfect and injudicious distribution of duties between the Health-Officer, City Physician, and Clerk of the Board of Health.

label: real
text: The Health-Officer shall be simply an intelligent and efficient executive officer, to superintend the prompt enforcement of all the laws and orders of the Board of Health.

label: real
text: The City Physician should keep at’ all times a free vaccine dispensary for the poor, and have the immediate charge or superintendence of such sick persons as came under the care and authority of the Health and Police Departments of the City Government.

label: real
text: And there should be a competent Clerk, who should perform the duties of Secretary to the Board of Health and the Health-Officer, and also the duties of Register of Vital Statistics.

label: real

label: real
text: ABSTRACT

label: real
text: Background and purpose: A brain tumour, especially a glioma, is a rare disease; it is challenging to treat and the prognosis is often poor.

label: real
text: Routine care includes surgery and concomitant chemoradiotherapy (CRT).

label: real
text: Diagnostic work-up and treatment effects are typically evaluated using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

label: real
text: Quantitative MRI (qMRI), unlike conventional MRI, has the advantage of providing tissue-specific relaxation rates and proton density.

label: real
text: The purpose is to detect changes in normal appearing white matter (NAWM) in brain tumour patients after CRT using qMRI.

label: real
text: Materials & methods: NAWM was analysed in 10 patients, in 83 MR examinations performed before and after surgery and after CRT.

label: real
text: Relaxation rates R1 and R2, the proton density (PD) and the concentration of myelin (cMy) were calculated from the qMRI scans and analysed in correlation to radiation dose and time after treatment.

label: real
text: Results: A significant decrease in cMy between pre-treatment imaging and first follow-up and an increase in PD were observed.

label: real
text: For low doses (less than 30 Gy) PD and cMy returned to baseline (=pre-operative status), while for high doses (>30 Gy) the change increased during the full extent of the follow-up period.

label: real
text: No difference could be established for R1.

label: real
text: For R2 an increase was observed during the first year, which then gradually returned to baseline.

label: real
text: For R2, stronger effects were seen as a consequence of higher absorbed doses.

label: real
text: Conclusion: In the long-term follow-up for glioma patients, qMRI is a powerful tool for detecting small changes, such as a decrease of myelin concentration, in NAWM after CRT.

label: real
text: Introduction

label: real
text: The most common types of brain tumours are gliomas, originating from the glial cells in the brain.

label: real
text: Depending on tumour type and malignancy grade, the prognosis varies, with a short overall survival for highgrade gliomas despite an aggressive treatment.

label: real
text: After surgery concomitant chemo radiotherapy (CRT) is given with the disadvantage that it affects the surrounding brain tissue as well as the targeted tumour.

label: real
text: Also, effects after surgery such as swelling and oedema can cause neurological symptoms and cognitive dysfunctions and these affects are therefore likely to have a long-term impact on quality of life.

label: real
text: Damage to the white matter in the brain is often observed within the first year, while radiation effects in the grey matter often do not occur until after six to 12 months.

label: real
text: Damage to the grey matter often involves vascular lesions such as telangiectasia and focal haemorrhages, while white matter damage is often transient demyelination.

label: real
text: The demyelination is a consequence of the irradiated oligodendrocytes going into apoptosis.

label: real
text: For brain tumours and therapy-related affects, MRI is the main imaging technique in clinical practice and includes several images such as T1W- and T2W-images, T2FLAIR, diffusion and perfusion.

label: real
text: Assessment of radiological findings is performed according to the RANO criteria (’Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Criteria for Gliomas’).

label: real
text: To improve imaging of brain tumours further, quantitative MRI (qMRI) has been proposed, as it provides more detailed and quantitative information about tumour properties.

label: real
text: One implementation of qMRI is the QRAPMASTER-sequence together with the SyMRI software.

label: real
text: This sequence is composed by a combination of interleaved slice selective saturation pulses, and multi echo readouts to generate imaging volumes with a range of echo- and saturation delay- times.

label: real
text: These can be used to calculate the qMRI maps; R1, R2 and PD (R1 = 1/T1, R2 = 1/T2).

label: real
text: The qMRI maps can be used for creating synthetic images.

label: real
text: It can also be used to determine myelin concentrations, a method which have been validated using Luxol fast blue staining.

label: real
text: A major advantage of the technique is the gain of quantitative and tissue specific values, and also the possibility to perform calculations and statistical tests on these.

label: real
text: A disadvantage is the variation of quantitative values depending on age and gender.

label: real
text: QMRI maps are also particularly useful for detecting contrast enhancement in peritumoural oedema.

label: real
text: Recent published work also concluded that qMRI can be useful for head and neck cancers.

label: real
text: The main aim of this project was to investigate if longitudinal qMRI imaging during follow-up after concomitant CRT can be used to detect changes in NAWM.

label: real
text: A second aim was to explore if such changes can be related to absorbed dose given in radiotherapy (RT), and if such changes vary over time.

label: real
text: The term qMRI will in the following text refer to quantitative values extracted with the QRAPMASTER sequence and SyMRI software.

label: real
text: IDEs are spatially nonlocal models (Lee et al. 2001) that are discrete in time and continuous in space.

label: real
text: They are especially useful for modeling the dynamics of species that have non-overlapping generations and distinct growth and dispersal stages (Kot and Schaffer 1986; Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: The basic IDE for a population with discrete and nonoverlapping generations is

label: real
text: nt+1 (x) = k (x, y) g [nt (y)] dy, (1)

label: real
text: where nt (x) is the population density in generation t at a spatial location x, is the spatial domain, k (x, y) is the dispersal kernel, and g [nt (y)] is the growth or recruitment function.

label: real
text: Population density is mapped from the current generation to the next in two distinct phases.

label: real
text: First, the population grows, while remaining fixed in space.

label: real
text: In particular, g [nt (y)] gives the new population-density at location y after growth has occurred.

label: real
text: After growth, individuals disperse, relocating from starting location y to new location x with probability governed by k (x, y).

label: real
text: The dispersal kernel is a probability density function for the final location x of the individuals.

label: real
text: In contrast to reaction–diffusion models, which are continuous in both time and space, IDE models account for seasonal growth and can incorporate a variety of dispersal patterns, including long-distance dispersal (Lewis et al. 2016).

label: real
text: The ability to choose a dispersal kernel that best fits the population being modeled is a key feature of IDEs.

label: real
text: As a result, IDE models have the advantage of increased ecological realism, as many species possess the features of seasonal growth and long-distance dispersal (Okubo and Levin 1989; Andersen 1991; Kot et al. 1996; Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: Despite the advantages of IDEs, these models have drawbacks as well.

label: real
text: IDEs can be computationally expensive since, as for most spatially nonlocal models, individuals may disperse long distances (Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: At the extreme end of this spatial complexity, under certain conditions, a propagule may start from any location in the spatial domain of the model and disperse to any other location in that domain.

label: real
text: In addition, it is often difficult to write down exact solutions for the equilibria or to perform general analytical explorations, except in certain special cases (Kot and Schaffer 1986; Zhou and Kot 2011; Bramburger and Lutscher 2019; Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: This analytic difficulty arises because finding equilibria amounts to finding functions that are fixed points of nonlinear integral equations.

label: real
text: Finally, most analyses of IDEs lack information about unstable equilibria, as unstable equilibria do not show up in standard numerical experiments.

label: real
text: While an argument may be made that it is more relevant to focus on (asymptotically) stable equilibria, in the interest of a complete characterization of the model it would be useful to observe all equilibria.

label: real
text: In order to circumvent some of these difficulties in analyzing IDE models, a number of tools have been developed to approximate or simplify the original model.

label: real
text: Special cases, such as an IDE model with a separable kernel or with the Laplace kernel, may allow for analytical results (Kot and Schaffer 1986; Zhou and Kot 2011; Bramburger and Lutscher 2019; Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: Other tools for analyzing IDE models involve

label: real
text: various approximations of the dispersal kernel, which can be used to approximate steady states and eigenvalues of IDEs, and may be employed for models with one or more species.

label: real
text: These methods include average dispersal-success (Van Kirk and Lewis 1997, 1999; Fagan and Lutscher 2006), modified average dispersal-success (Reimer et al. 2016), and geometric symmetrization (Kot and Phillips 2015; Phillips and Kot 2015; Rinnan 2018a, b; Marcinko 2020).

label: real
text: In this paper, we focus on an alternative for analyzing the population dynamics of a single species confined to a finite spatial domain.

label: real
text: In contrast to the methods discussed above, which approximate the dispersal kernel, we approximate the growth function.

label: real
text: Drawing inspiration from early work by Mark Lewis on the infinite-domain problem (Kot et al. 1996) and more recent developments by Otto (2017) and Nestor and Li (2022), we use a piecewise-constant function to approximate the growth function.

label: real
text: We refer to the IDE with this approximated growth as a block-pulse IDE.

label: real
text: An m-step block-pulse IDE has m terms, or steps, in the block-pulse approximation.

label: real
text: This terminology does not preclude using block-pulse approximations for the dispersal kernel as well; indeed, many applications of block-pulse methods for solving other integral problems involve approximating the entire integrand rather than a single component (Jiang and Schaufelberger 1992; Babolian et al. 2008).

label: real
text: The piecewise-constant nature of the growth function makes the block-pulse IDE simple and analytically tractable.

label: real
text: This formulation of the IDE removes many of the analytical barriers mentioned earlier and also offers numerical advantages.

label: real
text: With the increased tractability of the block-pulse IDE, we are able to obtain analytic expressions for both the iterates and the equilibria of the model.

label: real
text: Of particular interest, we gain explicit formulas for not only the stable but also the unstable equilibria of the block-pulse model.

label: real
text: The analytic formulas for the block-pulse equilibria involve a set of constants whose values are found by using a numerical root-finder to solve a finite, nonlinear set of implicit equations.

label: real
text: In other words, we use block-pulse IDEs as part of a hybrid analytical–numerical method for analyzing IDEs.

label: real
text: The numerical component, however, is small, and involves solving for a relatively small number of values.

label: real
text: Our method is thus more numerically efficient than a pure root-finding method for an operator equation, while the dominant analytic part of the method provides significant insight regarding model equilibria.

label: real
text: Furthermore, this method can be used for a broad set of growth functions, including growth functions with Allee effects.

label: real
text: An Allee effect, or depensation, occurs when a population’s per-capita recruitment increases, with density, at low densities (Allee et al. 1949; Lewis and Kareiva 1993).

label: real
text: Integrodifference equations with Allee effects have, historically, been challenging to analyze (Lutscher 2019).

label: real
text: However, the block-pulse method allows us to analyze both simple forms of growth, like compensatory growth, as well as challenging forms of growth, such as depensatory growth.

label: real
text: In Sect. 2, we look at block-pulse series and show how they can be used to approximate growth functions.

label: real
text: In Sect. 3, we describe the block-pulse IDE model and discuss assumptions and properties of the model, including a general, closed-form, analytic expression for the iterates of the spatial population-distributions.

label: real
text: In Sect. 4, we perform formal analyses of one-, two-, and three-step block-pulse IDEs and determine general patterns for these models.
